Implementation Plan

I've written the plan for #6335 below. It keeps only allowlisted diagnostic lines from artifact members before they are written to the evidence folder, and drops environment-assignment lines. It is ready for `/approved`.

One change goes beyond the literal answer to Q1. The existing `_ERROR_LINE_RE` only matches `##[error]`/`::error` lines, which editor stderr almost never contains. Using only the patterns named in Q1 would drop the very line (`Review isolation snapshot or transfer rejected`) that an existing contract test requires. So the plan adds a narrow error-keyword pattern for artifacts only. Two things weren't read during planning: the full layout of the `*summar*` members, and how the folder persists between stages.

---

## Implementation plan: issue #6335 (artifact credential disclosure in the heal evidence collector)

Planning ref: `git rev-parse HEAD` = `9d683d7cde74a04801fcd172011d81a68692cb24`, branch `claude/heal-evidence-bundle`. Integration branch metadata: `claude/heal-evidence-bundle`. No mismatch.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends extract_artifact_texts
Scope-mode justification: The finding is about one surface: artifact members that `extract_artifact_texts` / `Collector._collect_artifacts` copy verbatim, after only pattern redaction, into the evidence folder that model prompts read. Q1=A says to keep a structured, line-allowlisted extract per member and to drop environment-assignment lines. Q2=A says to leave job-log slicing (`slice_job_log`, the `slice-log` CLI and the failing step's env group) unchanged. The plan does both and nothing more. One small addition is included because the full fix is cheap: cached run metadata that predates the new format is re-fetched, so raw artifact copies from earlier collections cannot survive in the folder. It costs under 30 lines, adds no dependency and no external interface, and closes the "enter the evidence cache" part of the exploit (§6: Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed).

### Automation / wiring (§20.E)
- New script or extension: neither. Only existing code changes: `scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py`, its tests, and docs.
- Scheduler / PR-push entry point: unchanged. The `collect` subcommand already runs from the trusted evidence steps in `.github/workflows/clarify.yml`, `plan.yml` and `implement.yml` (on `issues` / `issue_comment` for trusted `ai:workflow-heal` issues). No workflow YAML edits, so the workflow size limit (§24) is unaffected.
- Long-running supervisor: none needed.
- DB work: none.
- `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry: none needed (no new script).

### 1. Files likely to change
- `scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py`: the allowlisted line extraction, the new-format check for cached metadata, and a docstring note.
- `tests/test_workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py`: new tests, plus one exact-content assertion that has to change.
- `agents.md`: one wording change in the workflow-heal evidence folder bullet (around line 211, "allowlisted artifact files").
- `changelog.d/6055-heal-evidence-bundle.md`: one bullet under `### For contributors`. HEAD 9d683d7 shows the convention on this stacked branch: fixes to unshipped heal-evidence code are folded into the 6055 fragment rather than added as a new fragment (CLAUDE.md §20, one fragment per PR).

### 2. Functions / modules to implement

In `scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py`:

**a. New module constants.** Each name was checked against the module's existing names (`_ERROR_LINE_RE`, `_DIAGNOSTIC_LINE_RE`, `_EXIT_CODE_RE`, `_SECRET_RES`, `MAX_DIAGNOSTIC_LINES`, `ARTIFACT_MEMBER_RES`); none collide.
- `ARTIFACT_EXTRACT_FORMAT = "allowlist-lines.v1"`
- `MAX_ARTIFACT_KEPT_LINES = 200` (the newest lines are kept, since errors usually come last)
- `MAX_ARTIFACT_LINE_CHARS = 400`
- `_ARTIFACT_ERROR_WORD_RE`: a narrow, case-insensitive error-keyword pattern for artifact stderr, which seldom has `##[error]` prefixes: `\b(?:error|errors|failed|failure|fatal|exception|traceback|panic|rejected|denied|timed out|timeout|killed|not found|exit(?:ed)? (?:code|status))\b`, plus `\brc=\d{1,3}\b`.
- `_ARTIFACT_STATUS_TOKEN_RE = ^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,39}$`. It applies only to `status_*` members, which hold a single token such as `success`, `pr_closed` or `skipped_budget` (written by `scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh`, for example at lines 4802 and 4935).
- `_ARTIFACT_ENV_ASSIGNMENT_RES`: deny patterns, checked before any keep rule. A line is dropped when any of these matches:
  1. A leading assignment: `^\s*(?:export\s+|declare\s+-\w+\s+|env\s+|set\s+)?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\s*=`.
  2. An assignment anywhere in the line whose name contains an uppercase letter: `\b[A-Za-z_]*[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_]*=` (for example `CUSTOM_SERVICE_PASSWORD=...` inside an error line).
  3. A `NAME=value` or `NAME: value` pair, quoted or not (JSON included), whose name contains `pass|pwd|secret|token|key|auth|cred|cookie|session|private|signature|bearer`, case-insensitive.
  4. URL userinfo: `://[^/\s:@]+:[^/\s@]+@`.

  Lowercase, non-secret keys such as `pr=`, `reason=`, `rc=` and `exit_code=` in our own stable log prefixes (`AUTOFIX_*`, `WORKFLOW_HEAL`) still pass.

**b. New `_artifact_diagnostic_extract(member_name: str, text: str) -> str`.**
1. Split into lines.
2. For each line: apply the deny patterns first. Then keep it if it matches `_ERROR_LINE_RE`, `_DIAGNOSTIC_LINE_RE`, `_EXIT_CODE_RE` or `_ARTIFACT_ERROR_WORD_RE`, or, for a `status_*` member only, if the stripped line matches `_ARTIFACT_STATUS_TOKEN_RE`.
3. Clip each kept line to `MAX_ARTIFACT_LINE_CHARS` and keep the last `MAX_ARTIFACT_KEPT_LINES`.
4. Return `# Extract (allowlist-lines.v1): kept K of N line(s); environment assignments and free-form text dropped (D line(s) denied)`, followed by `L<n>: <line>` rows. If nothing was kept, return the same header plus `(no allowlisted diagnostic lines)`.

**c. `extract_artifact_texts`.** The signature, the member filters (suffix, `member_re`, traversal, size and member caps) and the return shape `(safe_name, text)` stay the same. After `heal.sanitize_text(...)`, the text goes through `_artifact_diagnostic_extract(name, text)` and then `_clip_bytes(..., keep="tail")`. Raw member text is never returned. Update the docstring.

**d. `Collector._collect_artifacts`.**
- Before writing, remove existing `artifact-*` directories under `self.out / run_dir`. Resolve each path and check it stays inside `self.out`, the same pattern `collect_run` already uses to unlink stale `job-*.txt` files. This stops raw copies from an earlier collection from lingering.
- Set `meta["artifact_format"] = ARTIFACT_EXTRACT_FORMAT`.
- `_write` (which applies `redact_secrets` and the clip) and the UNTRUSTED header stay as they are. `redact_secrets` remains as defense in depth.

**e. `Collector.collect_run`, cache-reuse branch.**
- Reuse a cached `complete` meta only when `cached.get("artifact_format") == ARTIFACT_EXTRACT_FORMAT` or `cached.get("artifacts") == []`.
- Otherwise fall through to a fresh fetch. The rate-limit guard still applies: when `low_rate` is set, artifacts are skipped with `rate_limit_low` and the stale `artifact-*` dirs are removed, so nothing raw stays behind.

**f. Module docstring.** Add a short note near line 13 ("editor summaries, run summaries") that artifact members are reduced to allowlisted diagnostic lines.

Not touched (Q2=A): `slice_job_log`, `_cmd_slice_log`, `_job_diagnostics`, `render_structured_prompt_section`, `ARTIFACT_MEMBER_RES`.

### 3. Data structures affected
- Run `meta.json` gains one additive field, `artifact_format` (a string). Existing readers ignore unknown keys. `manifest.json` schema `workflow_failure_heal_evidence.v1` and `diagnostics.json` schema `workflow_failure_heal_diagnostics.v1` are unchanged.
- Each artifact file's content changes from redacted raw text to the line extract with a header. The path and naming (`runs/<repo>__<run>/artifact-<name>/<safe>`) are unchanged.

### 4. API / interface changes
- No CLI flags, env vars, log prefixes, file paths or schema names change. No new GitHub API calls (§14).
- The contents of `/evidence/runs/*/artifact-*/*` (clarify sandbox) shrink to allowlisted lines. Plan and implement already get only `diagnostics.json`, so their prompts are unchanged.

## Decisions

### D1 — Line allowlist with an artifact-specific error-keyword pattern
- Chosen: keep lines that match the existing `_ERROR_LINE_RE` / `_DIAGNOSTIC_LINE_RE` / `_EXIT_CODE_RE`, plus a narrow `_ARTIFACT_ERROR_WORD_RE`, plus status tokens for `status_*` members only.
- Alternatives considered: only the three existing patterns named in Q1 option A; dropping free-form members entirely (Q1 option B, rejected by the answer).
- Why: `_ERROR_LINE_RE` only matches `##[error]` / `::error` lines, which editor stderr rarely has. The existing contract test (`tests/test_workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py` around line 517) requires `Review isolation snapshot or transfer rejected` from `editor_attempt_1.err` to survive. Without the keyword pattern the extract would lose the evidence #6055 needed. This is still an allowlist of line shapes, not redaction of free-form text.

### D2 — Deny patterns run before keep patterns
- Chosen: any line with a leading assignment, an assignment whose name contains an uppercase letter, a secret-like key/value pair, or URL credentials is dropped, even if it also matches an error pattern.
- Alternatives considered: replacing the value with `[REDACTED]` (Q1 option C, explicitly rejected); dropping every line that contains `=`.
- Why: an error line can embed `CUSTOM_SERVICE_PASSWORD=...`, so deny-first fails closed. Lowercase non-secret keys such as `pr=`, `reason=` and `rc=` stay, because our stable diagnostic prefixes use them.

### D3 — Invalidate cached evidence that predates the new format
- Chosen: a format marker in `meta.json`, re-fetch when it is missing or dif
